thread:
Rajesh: Heads up — seeing a cluster of local NVMe badblocks on nodes backing gpu-pool p3d-usw2a. Provisioning failures started ~2h ago, ~8 nodes rejecting pod mounts with I/O errors. Heatmap looks concentrated to rack r3 in az us-west-2a.

Jess: Ugh. Any SMART output or dmesg snippets? Could be firmware or a bad batch. Also: are these ephemeral disks shared across tenants or dedicated to this pool?

Mike: quick paste from dmesg on node gpu-usw2-003: 

```
[ 12345.678901] nvme0n1: write faults, badblocks count=42
[ 12345.679012] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 4194304
[ 12346.000345] nvme nvme0: completion timeout
```

Jess: thanks. If we've got write faults and timeouts that's likely either controller FW or thermal/wear. What's the firmware on those drives?

Rajesh: checked — all affected nodes report controller fw 2.1.4-rc (we rolled that in last month). Heatmap (from disk-telemetry) shows wear leveling spikes coincident with GPU batch job windows. Could be a scheduling/IO pattern triggering accelerated write amplification.

infra-bot: [alert] ephemeral-cleaner failed on gpu-usw2-003: oom_kill invoked while running scratchfs scrub; job aborted. Error: killed by OOM killer.

Sam: ok, immediate triage plan: 1) cordon + drain the 8 nodes from p3d pool, 2) tag nodes with badblock=detected, 3) run non-destructive badblocks scan overnight (read-only) and full SMART long test on spare maintenance window, 4) open vendor RMA if SMART/long-test fails. Thoughts? :white_check_mark:

Jess: agree. One more thing — disable the nightly aggressive scrub until nodes are healthy; scrub + badblocks scans together will trash IO and may spark more timeouts. Also lower kube eviction thresholds on the pool to avoid mass reschedules.

Mike: tagging nodes now and kicking off a lightweight iostat to monitor in real time: 

```bash
kubectl get nodes -l gpu-pool=p3d -o name | xargs -n1 -I{} kubectl label {} nvme-issue=true --overwrite
for n in $(kubectl get nodes -l nvme-issue=true -o name); do ssh $n 'iostat -x 1 10' & done
```

Rajesh: good. I ran a quick smartctl snapshot on gpu-usw2-003: 

```
SMART overall-health self-assessment test: FAILED!
Device Model: ACME NVMe 5TB
Firmware Version: 2.1.4-rc
Data Units Written: 2,100,123,456
Percentage Used: 84%
Reallocated_Sector_Ct: 6
Warning: Badblock count increasing over last 24h
```

Sam: given percentage_used=84% and rising badblocks, vendor RMA looks likely. I'll open INF-4829 and attach logs. If RMA lead time > 72h we should plan node replacements (reprovision with fresh ephemeral) vs repair — cost decision: buy replacement drives vs reprovisioning and replace later. Leaning reprovision to reduce immediate downtime.

Jess: agree reprovisioning is faster. For long term: pause fw rollouts for controller fw 2.1.4-rc and freeze to last stable (2.0.9) until vendor confirms. Also add a telemetry rule to alert on "percentage_used > 80% and badblocks_growth > 5 in 24h".

Rajesh: Sam — can you run a non-destructive badblocks read-only pass on the tagged nodes tonight at 0100 UTC? I'll coordinate with scheduler to reduce batch jobs on p3d pool during the scan window.

Sam: yep — scheduling INF-4829 with scan task for 01:00 UTC. I'll also disable nightly scrub for the pool and lower kube eviction to 70% mem to stop thrash. Tagging @Jess for scrub disable. :thumbsup:

Jess: done — disabled aggressive scrub for gpu-pool p3d and adjusted eviction thresholds. Also added a temporary iops cap on that node group at 150k to avoid runaway write bursts while we investigate.

Mike: putting a one-off daemonset to collect /var/log/kern.log, nvme telemetry and iostat into the incident bucket. Command: 

```bash
kubectl apply -f https://git.internal/repro/daemons/nvme-trace.yaml
```

infra-bot: [info] INF-4829 created by Sam. Severity: P2. Attachments: dmesg snippets, smartctl output, node tags.

Rajesh: thanks all. Next steps: Sam runs the read-only badblocks at 01:00 UTC, Mike will stream iostat and kernel logs, Jess will freeze fw rollouts and keep scrub disabled. If tests confirm drive failures we'll RMA; if not, we'll look at scheduler IO patterns and add batching/caching mitigations in Optimize. :eyes:

Sam: I'll post results in this thread after the scan. :white_check_mark:
